children: Avanz Capital Egypt plans to set up a new investment company with as much as 3 billion Egyptian pounds ($60 million) in capital to back industrial businesses and support exports, as the private equity asset management firm expands its investments in the North African country.
The new vehicle, called Manara 2, is expected to launch in the first or second quarter of 2027, Managing Director Haytham Wagih said.
Avanz Capital Egypt is considering bringing local banks and insurance companies into the venture as potential investors, Wagih said.
“We are initially targeting capital of between 2.5 billion and 3 billion Egyptian pounds,” he said.
Manara 2 will target companies with growth potential across industries including agricultural processing, food, digital services, engineering, chemicals and ready-made garments, according to Wagih.
Avanz Capital Egypt has operated in the country since 2021 and currently manages Manara 1, an investment vehicle that invests in local companies and funds.

The company was previously affiliated with US-based Avanz Capital, which operates across several markets. A consortium comprising Egyptian financial advisory firm Exits MENA and Wagih signed an agreement last month to acquire Avanz Capital Egypt.
The transaction has received regulatory approval and is currently being implemented.
(Reporting by Safia Mounir; Editing by Shimaa Hefzi)
